svg.title: WordPress template hierarchy by request type
svg.desc: The template loader tests the query conditionals from top to bottom and stops at the first one that yields a template. Each row lists that request type's candidate template names from most to least specific, then the chain it falls back to, ending at index. Embeds use PHP templates only and fall back to the core embed template. Front page falls back to the home chain when the front page shows the latest posts and to the page chain when it is a static page; attachments fall back to the single chain. Each name is looked up as a block template (user-edited, then theme file, then plugin-registered) and as a PHP file in the child theme, then the parent theme.

g.text: Template hierarchy: first matching conditional wins, then first existing template
Each name is tried as a block template (templates/NAME.html, or a wp_template post edited in the Site Editor) and as NAME.php,
first in the child theme, then in the parent theme. Block template sources: user-edited, then theme file, then plugin-registered.
A block template wins over a PHP file of equal or lower specificity. {term} and {slug} are tried decoded, as slug, then as ID.
Purple: the template picked in the editor (_wp_page_template). index is always the last resort; a block theme must ship index.html.
